text: Chapter 10 says a debugger's most useful question is not "what does this do" but something else. What?
choices: "What exactly did I expect, and what exactly happened instead?" - because the gap between those two is the bug.
"What changed since it last worked?", since most bugs are introduced by recent edits.
"Can I reproduce it reliably?", since an intermittent fault cannot be diagnosed.
"Which line threw the exception?", since the stack trace localises the fault.
explanation: The other three are genuinely useful and all are downstream of the first. Without an explicit expectation there is no gap to measure — you are looking at output with no standard to compare it against, which is why "it doesn't work" is not yet a bug report. The preface asks for this habit and Chapter 35 says it is the single thing most worth keeping from the book.
